The check passes today (`13 passed` with `-W error::DeprecationWarning`), yet the transcript without that flag shows the warnings are still present (`13 passed, 2 warnings`). This means the check cannot discriminate "done" from "untouched" — it already reports success before any work is performed. The issue describes a test-scoped `filterwarnings` ignore or similar suppression as the fix, but whatever mechanism is already in place makes the strict check pass now. A valid check would need to verify the warnings are absent from normal test output (e.g., `uv run pytest ... -q 2>&1 | grep -c DeprecationWarning` returning 0, which currently returns 2).
